correctness.rationale: The strict separation condition resets each upper visit below the switch; in a lower run the positive ratio y/x^p grows by lambda^(1-p), so visits recur. For q=1/lambda and a=1-lambda*x_tau, the first upper iterate after the reset is the least integer m with (p-1)m>tau+1+log_q(a^p/y0). The resulting tau'=(p/(p-1))*tau+O(1) is uniform along the fixed orbit. Dividing by successive powers of R=p/(p-1) and summing the bounded-error tail gives a limit and an O(1) unscaled error. The limit is positive since tau tends to infinity and the remaining tail from any visit in units of that visit is bounded by K/(R-1). Inversion gives the log count. At p=2, a tends to 1 strictly from below after the first visit, so floor(log_q(a^2/y0)) is eventually ceil(log_q(1/y0))-1, including at integer log heights. This argument applies only with positive initial height and without equality hits under the stated separation condition.
correctness.reproduction: Independent replay: use Python Fraction for lambda=1/5, x=1/2, y=1/25; at each integer time starting at 0 record the time if y>x*x, reject equality, and simultaneously update (x,y) to (1-lambda*x,lambda*y) if upper or (lambda*x,lambda*y) otherwise. The first ten visit times are 2,8,20,44,92,188,380,764,1532,3068. Initial (2/3,1/125) gives 3,11,27,59,123,251,507,1019,2043,4091; (1/2,1/10) gives 1,6,16,36,76,156,316,636,1276,2556. No equality was encountered in those finite runs. The supplied checker was inspected as evidence, not run; finite trajectories do not establish the asymptotic or boundary-hit exclusion for all time.
